entities.summary: Jean de Roquetaillade, also known as John of Rupescissa, was a French Franciscan alchemist and eschatologist who played a pivotal role in the medieval alchemical tradition. Born in France around 1310, de Roquetaillade was a key figure in the development of Hermeticism, a philosophical and spiritual movement that sought to reconcile Christian theology with ancient Greek and Roman wisdom. His magnum opus, 'The Book of the Hierarchies of Hierarchies,' is considered one of the most important works of medieval alchemy. De Roquetaillade's eschatological writings, particularly his 'Tractatus de Passione Domini,' influenced the development of Christian mysticism and the medieval understanding of the apocalypse. Through his alchemical and theological pursuits, de Roquetaillade contributed significantly to the intellectual and spiritual landscape of medieval Europe.
